findings.evidence: Triggered by "ai-kit-spec-review", "review my spec/plan", naming one of these frameworks alongside a spec/plan/design review, or passing document path(s).
findings.fix: Use when a design, specification, requirements, RFC, or implementation plan needs a framework-aware review, with fixes when the user authorizes them. Dispatches clean-context reviewers, optionally across AI runtimes, and routes authorized revisions through the relevant framework or a fixer. Supports superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, and generic documents. Use for requests such as "review my spec" or "review and fix this plan," including document paths supplied for review. Not for code or pull-request reviews, writing a new plan, or configuring reviewers.

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 511 lines, exceeding the 500-line progressive-disclosure limit.
findings.fix: Keep the essential routing and safety rules in SKILL.md and move detailed, conditionally needed dispatch or surface-message guidance into an existing appropriately triggered reference, preserving the procedures and their links.

findings.evidence: "Your job: drive a review-and-fix loop" applies even though the skill is invocable "by asking to review a spec/plan".
findings.fix: Distinguish review-only requests from requests that authorize revisions. On review-only requests, dispatch and surface the findings without invoking any fixer or framework rewrite; ask before editing when the user's intent is unclear.

findings.evidence: When git rev-parse fails for a document outside any repo, the fallback says to run git worktree list and match the document to a worktree, but gives no outcome when that also fails.
findings.fix: Define the outside-repository branch explicitly: ask the user for a grounding directory or stop with an actionable message; if supporting it, pass the confirmed directory and disclose that the runner cannot verify the review's read-only contract outside Git.

findings.evidence: The single-reviewer surface message gives a report path, but Cleanup removes $RUN_TMP_DIR after approval, deleting that report.
findings.fix: For approved single-reviewer runs, either retain the reported artifact at a stable path or omit the report path from the surface message before removing the temporary directory.
